messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: precompilation and densities
parts:
I've been wondering how big the object file would be
if we precompiled everything in math other than the
densities.

And we might be able to deal with densities for
the most part with this pattern:

template <typename T, typename U>

return_type<T, U>::type
exponential(const T& y, const T& alpha) {

VectorView<T, ...> y_vec(y);
VectorView<U, ...> alpha_vec(alpha);

return exponential_vec(y_vec, alpha_vec);
}

Then we could precompile exponential_vec for the combos
we need (double, integer, other) where other is var
or fvar<T>, so that's just 3^N for N arguments for reverse
mode (and another 3^N for each other autodiff instantiation).
Still 81 for student-T, but it's not the tens of thousands we
get from all the ways a vector view can be constructed.
Even the VectorView instances can be precompiled here --- there
aren't that many.

- Bob
